clue.text: Novelist in Breton resort

indicators.note: to re-sort something is to sort it again, putting its letters into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written: the adjective for Brittany

explanation.surface: A writer is spotted holidaying at a seaside town in Brittany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday town to go with 'Breton', but it is a verb telling you to re-sort the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte, Emily and Anne were the three famous Victorian sisters who each wrote celebrated books.

clue.text: Slangily, 'money', to begin with, is called by American ‘cabbage’

indicators.note: to begin with points at the opening letter of each of the next words only

blocks.note: brass is British slang for money
the opening letters of these two words
A is the standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: An American is said to call money 'cabbage' in slang, which is true enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabbage' really is US slang for money, which makes the surface plausible; here it is the plain vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Brassica is the botanical genus that includes cabbages, kale, broccoli and sprouts.

clue.text: Doubt oar will be seen moving, having this kind of motor?

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift about from their written positions into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rower who doubts the oars will be needed, since the boat has a motor.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor clamped to the stern of a small boat, outside the hull, is described with this term.

clue.text: Resort with low-priced rent and sought-after square

indicators.note: rent here is the past tense of rend, so the words are torn apart and put back differently

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An estate agent's advert for a holiday town with cheap rents and a fashionable town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid for housing; it is the past tense of rend, meaning torn.
explanation.definitionFit: On a Scrabble board, the red squares that multiply a whole word's points threefold are the most coveted spaces.

clue.text: At end of Inferno, T. Hanks reveals ‘I’d rather not’

indicators.note: the letters sit at the tail of one word and run on into the following name

blocks.note: the final two letters of the first word joined to the initial and surname

explanation.surface: Tom Hanks, at the close of the film Inferno, admits he would prefer not to do something.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Hanks starred in the 2016 film Inferno; ignore the punctuation and read straight through.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are polite ways of declining an offer or refusing something.

clue.text: Monster’s rising, so ...

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, meaning so

explanation.surface: A monster is getting up, so... and the sentence trails off in suspense.
explanation.definitionFit: A folk-tale giant who eats people is a classic fairy-story beast.

clue.text: Struggling to make headway, surrender having lost energy in drawn-out conflict

indicators.note: struggling suggests thrashing about, so the letters wrestle into a new order
having lost tells you a letter is dropped from the word just before

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An army bogged down, unable to advance, gives up in a long war.
explanation.walkthrough: One E goes from surrender, leaving SURRNDER to mix with HEADWAY.
explanation.definitionFit: The series of English and French wars from 1337 to 1453 actually lasted well over a century.

clue.text: One who’s disinvested in stud rearing

indicators.note: a rearing horse throws itself about, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An investor pulls money out of a horse-breeding stud farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disinvested' reads as financial, but split it as dis-invested: the opposite of vested, so wearing no clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist goes without clothing, playfully described as having had their vest taken off.

clue.text: Seen in Jaws, a distressing monster

indicators.note: seen in says the letters are visible inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the last letter of the film title, the article, and the start of the adjective

explanation.surface: A film critic notes that the shark in Jaws is a frightening creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes pleasure in cruelty can be called a monster in the figurative, human sense.

clue.text: Get a coach with time for run

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one letter stands where another was

blocks.note: taken as written
to coach someone is to train them
T is the abbreviation for time
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Hire a coach with enough time to fit in a run.
explanation.walkthrough: The R of TRAIN is swapped for a T.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach or achieve a goal is to get there, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Did I rant about W Indies? Partly

indicators.note: about suggests moving round, so the letters are turned around into another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone worries whether they went on too long about the West Indies, and admits they partly did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partly' seems to answer the question, but it belongs to the definition: a part of the West Indies.
explanation.definitionFit: This Caribbean island, twinned with Tobago, is one portion of the West Indies archipelago.

clue.text: A small modern-day country; a vast ancient kingdom

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a present-day Middle Eastern nation

explanation.surface: A history lesson contrasting a little modern nation with a huge empire of old.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mesopotamian empire centred on Nineveh dominated much of the Near East around 700 BC.

clue.text: Notice bar is very clean

blocks.note: to spot something is to notice it
bar as a preposition means except, as does less

explanation.surface: A sign announces that the pub is immaculate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice' and 'bar' look like nouns, a sign and a pub; here they are a verb and a preposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without a single mark or stain is perfectly clean.

clue.text: Disasters when cakes without filling rise internally

indicators.note: without filling means the inside letters are emptied out, leaving only the shell
internally says the next piece goes inside the shell just made

blocks.note: just the first and last letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A baker's catastrophe: unfilled cakes swelling up inside the oven.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergencies and calamities are times of acute trouble, the plural of crisis.

clue.text: Depending on duplicity

blocks.note: re means about or concerning, as does on
telling untruths is a form of deceit

explanation.surface: Someone whose success hinges on deceit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depending on' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'Depending' and 'on' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: If you are counting on someone, you are leaning on or trusting them, so the participles match.

clue.text: Banger that’s gone off to get masked, ultimately, with flavouring

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: in British slang a banger is an old, rundown car (it is also a sausage)
something that has gone off has left
to get a point is to see it
the closing letter

explanation.surface: A sausage that has gone bad is being disguised with seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banger' and 'gone off' suggest a spoiled sausage, but the banger is a clapped-out car and 'gone off' means departed.
explanation.definitionFit: These aromatic seeds from a plant in the parsley family are used to flavour bread and cakes.

clue.text: With shrewdness, Anglo-Saxon king oversees bishopric

indicators.note: in a down clue, oversees means one part sits on top of the next

blocks.note: AS is the standard abbreviation for Anglo-Saxon
the familiar short name of the boy pharaoh Tutankhamun
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire and the seat of a bishop

explanation.surface: A cunning early English monarch keeps an eye on a diocese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anglo-Saxon king' reads as one person, but the king is Egyptian and Anglo-Saxon is a separate abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting cleverly and with sharp judgment is acting in a canny, perceptive manner.

clue.text: Circulates stripped resin scent?

definitions.note: read whole, the clue describes what the plural noun does: fragrant gum burnt to spread its smell

indicators.note: things that circulate move round, so the letters go round into a new order
stripped means the outer layer is taken off, losing the first and last letters

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wafts the smell of burning resin around a room.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer R and T are dropped before the remaining letters are mixed; the whole clue then doubles as a description of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Frankincense and similar gums burnt for their fragrant smoke are aromatic substances made from tree sap.

clue.text: Clever, removing top to add interest when showering often

indicators.note: removing top means the word's first letter is taken off

blocks.note: a clever person is brainy
to season food is to make it more interesting with spice

explanation.surface: A smart person takes off their hat to make things interesting while frequently taking showers.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of the year in tropical climates when downpours are frequent is the monsoon period.

clue.text: Everyman's quietly guarded, oddly absent ... and lewd

indicators.note: with the odd-numbered letters gone, only the second, fourth and sixth are kept

blocks.note: Everyman is the setter, who refers to themself as I; 's stands for am
p is the musical marking piano, meaning quietly
the even-placed letters

explanation.surface: The setter confesses to being discreet, rather odd, absent-minded and a bit smutty.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecent or unchaste thoughts are morally unclean, a sense the adjective has long carried.

clue.text: Pathetic jerk undertakes banter

indicators.note: undertakes means takes on, so one word takes another inside it

blocks.note: a tic is an involuntary twitch or jerk
to rag someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: A sad idiot takes on some teasing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' reads as an insult for a person; here it is a muscle twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pitiful or deeply sad, arousing pity, is the sense both words share.

clue.text: Soft ground buried in tremor assault

indicators.note: buried in says the letters lie concealed within the words that follow

blocks.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: During an earthquake attack, something sinks into soft earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A bog or swamp is waterlogged land into which one sinks.

clue.text: Being waited on, eating starter of chicken with pastry casing

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its opening letter
eating means taking something inside, so one piece swallows the other

blocks.note: a traveller on the way is being awaited at their destination
just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A diner being served by a waiter eats a chicken first course wrapped in pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waited on' suggests restaurant service, but it means awaited: someone on their way.
explanation.definitionFit: This French cooking term describes food such as beef Wellington baked wrapped in a crust.

clue.text: Eyesore ... by the sound of it!

indicators.note: by the sound of it says to go by how a word is pronounced rather than written

blocks.note: a pigsty is a classic eyesore, and the word for it is pronounced the same

explanation.surface: Someone points at an ugly sight and says it sounds just like what it is.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Eyesore' two ways: a sore on the eye, and an ugly sight like a pigsty.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflamed swelling on the eyelid is quite literally a sore on the eye.

clue.text: Got bogus knocked off womenswear

indicators.note: knocked off suggests being knocked out of shape, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone bought fake clothing that turned out to be a counterfeit knock-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked off' fits the surface as counterfeit goods; here it signals mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheepskin boots from Australia were hugely popular as a women's fashion item in the 2000s.

clue.text: Duke's seen for a time in online messages with posh clothing

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one letter replaces another in the word

blocks.note: short posts on the platform formerly called Twitter
D is the abbreviation for Duke
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An aristocrat posts on social media for a while, pictured in smart clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: One T of TWEETS, the second, gives way to a D.
explanation.definitionFit: Suits of woollen cloth are traditional country wear of the British upper classes.

clue.text: Gave up half of one’s ground

indicators.note: half of means only one of the two halves of the word is kept

blocks.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
food ground with the teeth has been chewed

explanation.surface: Someone surrendered half their land in a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like land; it is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain from or deliberately avoid something is to forgo it, so both are past-tense verbs of renouncing.

clue.text: Fermented refreshments obviating yolks; ordinarily subzero ... primarily?

definitions.text: Fermented refreshments obviating yolks; ordinarily subzero ... primarily?

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so each preceding word gives only its opening letter

blocks.clueFragment: Fermented refreshments obviating yolks; ordinarily subzero
blocks.note: the initials of the six words

explanation.surface: A description of cultured, egg-free desserts usually served frozen.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: frozen yoghurt is fermented, made without egg yolks, and served below freezing.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen yoghurts are cultured dairy treats, unlike custard-based ice cream, and are kept cold.
